title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.21577v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers. However, tool metadata used for discovery and selection is not, by itself, necessarily bound to a verified provider identity. This paper studies this gap as tool-provider misbinding: a failure in which a request intended for a legitimate provider is instead resolved to an attacker-controlled tool. The attacker does not compromise the host, LLM, legitimate server, or network channel; it only operates another MCP server that advertises tools with chosen metadata. We formulate tool provider misbinding as an attacker-controlled tool-selection optimization problem and evaluate it in a controlled MCP environment across five LLM-based clients. translated_title: 当工具名称不等于身份：测量基于MCP的AI代理中的提供商错误绑定
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）应用日益以智能代理的形式运行，自主选择并调用外部工具。模型上下文协议（MCP）通过允许客户端组合由多个服务器提供的工具，对这种交互进行了标准化。然而，用于发现和选择的工具元数据本身并不一定绑定到经过验证的提供商身份。本文将这一安全空白作为“工具提供商错误绑定”问题进行研究：这是一种故障情形，即原本发送给合法提供商的请求反而被解析到攻击者控制的工具。在此攻击中，攻击者并未入侵主机、LLM、合法服务器或网络通道，而只是运行另一个MCP服务器，该服务器用自选的元数据来发布工具。作者将工具提供商错误绑定形式化为一个攻击者可控的工具选择优化问题，并在受控的MCP环境中对五个基于LLM的客户端进行了评估。结果表明，交互行为是驱动错误绑定的关键因素。（注：原摘要在此处似乎不完整，"The strongest"之后的文字被截断。）
tldr: 本文揭示了基于MCP的AI代理中的“工具提供商错误绑定”安全漏洞：攻击者无需入侵主机、LLM、合法服务器或网络通道，仅通过运行另一个发布自选元数据工具的MCP服务器，就能让发给合法提供商的请求被解析到攻击者控制的工具，并将其形式化为攻击者可控的工具选择优化问题，在五个LLM客户端上进行了实证评估。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies and measures tool-provider misbinding in MCP-based AI agents, showing that an attacker can redirect requests intended for legitimate providers to attacker-controlled tools merely by operating another MCP server advertising tools with chosen metadata—without compromising the host, LLM, legitimate server, or network—formalized as an attacker-controlled tool-selection optimization problem and evaluated across five LLM-based clients.
